_anchors.canvas.w: 66, and it is MEASURED rather than estimated. Every one of the twelve yaw bands of both clips was rendered and its ink bounded: the widest reaches 29 px either side of the axis. 33 leaves four. The first build guessed 56 at the authored scale and carried the guess through 1.76 to 100, which rastered nearly twice the pixels it drew — nine seconds a page load, on a shelf whose whole surface is edit-refresh-look.
_anchors.canvas.h: 90: the ink runs 36 px above the core and 48 below across all twelve bands and both clips, measured the same way. 41 above and 49 below leaves five and one — the tight side is the feet, which are the one place a plant cannot move.
_anchors.canvas.originX: 33, dead centre — the axis every yaw band turns about. Off-centre would swing the machine out of its own cell between bands.
_anchors.canvas.originY: 41. The core, which is the bone the boost pitches and rolls about; the measured 36 px of cannon and crest sit above it.
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 5, the 15/08 idiom. Facets need range, not more levels — the range is in the palette.
_anchors.light.y: -0.68, high and hard. A hangar lamp, not a sun: PS1 mechs are lit from above with little bounce, and a high key is what makes adjacent facets differ.
_anchors.light.z: -0.4, well toward the viewer — MORE front light than any subject here. A facet only reads if the plate facing the camera differs from the plates either side of it, and a grazing lamp would put both in shadow.
_anchors.light.curve: 1.25. Near the crypt's 1.3: the dark end compresses so the machine sits against a lit floor with real contrast, the era's own look.
_anchors.outline.enabled: true, the 15/08 ink verdict. It also does a second job here: fixed-function hardware had no anti-aliasing, so a hard edge IS the period read.
_anchors.outline.material: "ink", cool near-black — a hangar is lit blue and a warm line would float off the metal.
_anchors.outline.inner: true, and Part.weld places it: plate against plate inside one section is one surface; every section boundary keeps its seam, which is what makes a machine read as assembled.
_anchors.body.scale: **1.76, and the number is his colleague's verdict compiled.** *"Mechas grandes na tela"*: the machine now draws 60 px in a 180 px frame — a third of its height, against 34 px in 150 and a fifth of it before. It is also what makes the facet legible at all: a plate on a 34 px body was three pixels across and had no room to crease. Derived, not chosen — 30 world units x focal 156 / camDist 78 = 60 px, and 60 / 34 model units = 1.76.
_anchors.texture.dither: 0 on the body — the skate round's measured rule. Even at 60 px the plates are single-material and a weave would fight the facet creases; the arena's floor is where the lattice goes.
_anchors.texture.facet: **2, and this file is the first in the project to spend the knob.** Each normal component snaps to halves, so the machine shades as a small set of flat plates with hard creases between them — one normal per face, which is what the hardware his reference remembers actually did. 3 was measured smoother and 2 reads as polygons; the number is the PS1 idiom itself, so it is a knob his verdict can move.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 8, one more than the deepest mass (the core at 5.2 half-depth).
_anchors.shadow.strength: 3 ramp steps — the DEEPEST on the shelf. Hard shadows are the other half of the era's look, and a machine of plates casts them on itself constantly.
_anchors.fill.y: 0.2, barely from below: a hangar floor bounces little.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.08, the LOWEST here. A fill blends two lambert terms and blending is exactly what a facet must not do — too much and the creases soften back into a gradient.
_anchors.gait.depth: 8 px: the limb radius the yaw decomposition multiplies a rotation by, measured off this body — the thigh runs 7.8 and the shin 8.2.
_anchors.gait.roll: 0.2, matching gait.swing — and it is not a clip that rolls. The EXACT yaw decomposition writes the out-of-plane half of every limb swing as a roll companion, and a companion needs an amplitude to be expressed in; equal amplitudes make the conversion a ratio of one. The walk itself authors no roll track, which is still the null case: at band 0 the decomposition emits none.
_anchors.frames.walk: 4, and the low count is period-correct rather than a saving: the machines of that era animated in few hard poses. Four named phases at the quarters need a multiple of four, and 4 is the smallest legal one.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.2 turn = 72 degrees at a key of 1. The walk's largest key is 0.62 on a thigh, which is 45 degrees — a heavy machine's stride. DERIVED from this body, not carried: run 7 lost a limb to exactly that carry.
_anchors.gait.lift: 3 px. The core drops 1.6 on each plant and rises 0.9 between: impact, not bounce.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 130: four frames make a 520 ms stride, about two steps a second for a machine this size. Read by the bench; in the arena the stride advances with distance.
